title: 3854. Minimum Operations to Make Array Parity Alternating

examples.explanation: Applying the following operations: Increase nums[2] by 1, resulting in nums = [-2, -3, 2, 4]. Decrease nums[3] by 1, resulting in nums = [-2, -3, 2, 3]. The resulting array is parity alternating, and the value of max(nums) - min(nums) = 3 - (-3) = 6 is the minimum possible among all parity alternating arrays obtainable using exactly 2 operations.

Applying the following operation: Decrease nums[1] by 1, resulting in nums = [0, 1, -2]. The resulting array is parity alternating, and the value of max(nums) - min(nums) = 1 - (-2) = 3 is the minimum possible among all parity alternating arrays obtainable using exactly 1 operation.
No operations are required. The array is already parity alternating, and the value of max(nums) - min(nums) = 7 - 7 = 0, which is the minimum possible.

hints: A parity alternating array must follow one of two patterns: even, odd, even, ... or odd, even, odd, ....
If a position has the wrong parity, its value must be changed by exactly +/-1 (one operation) to fix the parity.
For each pattern, count the minimum operations needed to make all positions match the required parity.
Among patterns with minimum operations, choose adjustments that minimize max(nums) - min(nums) while preserving parity.
